standard.title: Sound
standard.description: explore different actions to make sounds and how to make a variety of sounds, and recognise that sound energy causes objects to vibrate
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have informally experienced sound. They have not yet investigated the relationship between actions, vibration and sound production, or explored how sound can be varied (louder, softer, higher, lower).
standard.progression_endpoint: Students describe how different actions (striking, blowing, plucking, scraping, shaking) produce sounds, explain that sound energy causes objects to vibrate, and investigate how to vary sound properties including loudness and pitch.

nodes.label: Sound is produced by different actions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and describe different actions that produce sound, classify instruments or objects by the action used to produce their sound, and explain that all sound production involves some form of action on an object.
nodes.minimum_width: Students name at least four different sound-producing actions and give one example of each.
nodes.typical_width: Students explore different ways to produce sound (striking, blowing, scraping, plucking, shaking); classify instruments by action type; explore how traditional musical instruments used by First Nations Australians produce their characteristic sounds; and design and make simple instruments that produce sounds.
wider: Explore how traditional musical instruments used by First Nations Australians produce their characteristic sounds — examining action-to-sound relationships in culturally specific instruments
Design and make instruments that produce different sounds — applying sound production knowledge in a design context
Explore how voices have a unique sound and investigate voice-activated tools — connecting voice pattern recognition to everyday technology

response_modes.reason: First Nations instrument direction and instrument design provide culturally rich and creative directions that build a broader repertoire of action-to-sound relationships, enriching the concept before N2 applies the vibration mechanism across those same contexts.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations instrument direction is elaboration-grounded and culturally rich. Instrument design provides a genuine creative application of sound production knowledge.
success_criteria: Names at least four different actions that produce sound with an example of each
Classifies at least three instruments or objects by the action used to produce their sound

nodes.label: Sound energy causes objects to vibrate
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain that sound energy causes objects to vibrate, observe and describe vibrations produced by sound-making objects, and connect the speed or strength of vibration to sound properties.
nodes.minimum_width: Students describe vibrations in at least one sound-making object and explain that the object is vibrating because of sound energy.
nodes.typical_width: Students observe vibrations from a twanged ruler, tuning fork or music speaker; explain that sound energy causes vibrating; investigate how the speed or strength of vibration relates to loudness or pitch; and describe how sound travels through different materials — connecting vibration to hearing.
wider: Investigate which materials best muffle sound — examining how different materials absorb or block vibrations
Discuss situations where students have heard echoes and explore how animals (dolphins, bats) use echolocation — connecting sound vibration to navigation
Explore how music can be understood as patterns of sounds — connecting vibration to the structured organisation of sound in music (AC9S2H01)

response_modes.reason: Students commonly believe sound is simply noise rather than energy that causes physical vibration. Making the vibration mechanism explicit — sound energy → object vibrates → vibration travels through medium → detected as sound — is the key conceptual scaffold before students can explain how sound behaves in different materials or conditions.

success_criteria: Describes vibrations in a named sound-making object
Explains that the object vibrates because of sound energy
